thread:
alex: :rotating_light: Pager: economy-tier p99 latency spiking in eu-west (alerts: p99 > 1200ms, error-rate small increase). I'm opening a thread — seeing drop in throughput from a few large customers and a backlog in the economy lane.
ops-bot: Incident runbook triggered: ECONOMY_LATENCY_SPIKE. Paging @maria (oncall), @ken (runtime), @sam (routing).
maria: Ack. Oncall here, looking. Can someone paste the top traceroute/stack traces? Also: which customers impacted and is it causing 429s or 503s?
alex: Quick snapshot: top offending route is /v1/generate with model redwood-small-8k-econ pinned. 5 customers show increased queue times; we have elevated tail latency in eu-west-2a nodes. Errors currently mostly timeouts to the backend serving pool, not 5xx from runtime.
ken: I'm seeing KV cache pressure and increased batching stalls on a subset of hosts. Suspect a bad shard of dedicated pool got noisy garbage collection + longer kernel latencies. Noticing memory juggling and slow GPU-to-CPU copies on a few kernels.
sam: Given this looks pool-localized, I'd prefer traffic shaping rather than full-scale blackout. Propose: 1) apply a temporary holdback on economy tier in eu-west (reduce econ share by ~40%), 2) steer incremental portion to nearby region (us-east) for customers with cross-region opt-in, 3) enable rate cap at route level for the heaviest customers to keep fairness.
irene: Customer impact: two mid-market tenants reported 2–3 min blips causing degraded UX; no major enterprise outages yet. Ops alerting shows spike at 12:07 UTC, persists.
maria: Agreed with Sam. Plan: canary change first (10% split) then 40% if stable. Also prepare a fallback to re-enable economy full traffic if we see regressions. I'll own the change and rollback.
ken: Commands to update smart-routing policy (internal API):
```
# canary 10% economy -> us-east
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/redwood/v1/routing/modify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_KEY" \
  -d '{"policy_id":"routing-economy-eu-west","actions":[{"type":"split","percent":10,"target_region":"us-east-1"}]}'
```
sam: For per-customer throttles (quick blunt tool):
```
# rate limit customer A to 50 req/min on /v1/generate
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/redwood/v1/quotas" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_KEY" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"cust-0192","route":"/v1/generate","limit":50}'
```
maria: Executing canary now. Will monitor traces, queue length, and p99 on the econ lane. I will post checkpoints.
ops-bot: Change request accepted: routing-economy-eu-west -> split 10% -> us-east-1. Change id: ch_20260315_001. Automatic rollback window: 5m if p99 increases.
alex: Noted. Alert channels: #incidents (this thread) and #eng-runtime for visibility.
maria: +30s: canary applied. Observability: slight drop in local queue depth, p99 dipped to ~980ms (from 1220ms). No new 5xx. Traces show the canary traffic is hitting us-east pools.
sam: Okay wait for 3–5 min. If stable, push 40% shift.
irene: Customer reports: Tenant-7 still seeing minor slowdowns (retries), but overall fewer timeouts. We're not seeing spike in cross-region auth failures.
ken: FYI we also patched a kernel path (hotfix queued) but not promoted yet; avoiding rolling that across the pool until traffic stabilizes.
maria: +4m: metrics stable. Increasing split to 40%.
ops-bot: Change request accepted: routing-economy-eu-west -> split 40% -> us-east-1. Change id: ch_20260315_002.
alex: Heads-up: enabling 40% will increase cost exposure for this mitigation. We should note cost impact for post-incident review.
maria: Applied 40%. Immediate telemetry: p99 down to ~540ms on eu-west economy lane, overall platform p99 improved. Some added latency for steered requests due to cross-region RTT but within SLO for those customers that opt-in.
sam: I'm enabling temporary per-route rate caps for the three heaviest tenants in eu-west to prevent queue reaccumulation. Commands executed.
ken: Observing improved memory pressure and reduced batching stalls on the previously noisy hosts.
irene: Customer update: Tenant-7 reported recovery. Tenant-3 still at edge but degraded calls reduced from 15% to 2%.
alex: Let's keep an eye on error budget and cost. Maria, set a note summarizing mitigation and ETA to hand off to next oncall.
maria: Will do. Drafting handoff: "Mitigation: 40% economy traffic steered to us-east for eu-west traffic; per-customer rate caps applied to top three heavy tenants; kernel hotfix staged but not yet rolled. Monitor p99 and queue depth. If p99 < 700ms for 15m, demote incident to watch. Rollback plan: revert split to 0% and remove rate caps. Owner: maria. Next oncall: ken (in 2h)."
ken: I'll take the handoff in 2h. Also request logs for the noisy hosts to investigate GC/kernel pattern next shift.
maria: Adding runbook note to ticket and closing pager if numbers hold. Re-opening if p99 increases or error-rate > 1%.
ops-bot: Incident status: MITIGATED -> WATCHING. ch_20260315_001,ch_20260315_002 applied. Incident runbook updated. Pager closed at 12:20 UTC.
alex: Great job. Postmortem owners: ken (root cause allocation), sam (routing policy behavior), maria (mitigation timeline + ops notes). Please save links to dashboards in the ticket.
irene: I'll draft a short customer-facing note for Tenant-7 and Tenant-3: explaining cross-region mitigation and invite them to opt-in for cross-region fallback in future.
maria: Handing off to ken now. Leaving the split at 40% and rate caps active. I'll be reachable if it toggles.
ken: Taking handoff. I'll dig into kernel traces and prepare the targeted hotfix rollouts for the affected hosts once we confirm the regression pattern. If anything regresses I'll revert the split immediately.
sam: Thanks all. Quick retrospective: consider automated templated policy to do econ-tier bifurcation under similar signals to reduce manual time next incident.
alex: Added to ops backlog. Closing thread after ticket update.
pager-duty: Incident closed in pager system. Reference id: INC-20260315-0483."
